title: CBRN: High Angle Rope Rescue
description: U.S. Marines with Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear Defense Platoon, Headquarters Battalion, 3rd Marine Division conduct high-angle inserts to assess simulated chemical or radiological threats at Camp Hansen, Okinawa, Japan, August 15, 2019. CBRN Marines executed simulated site exploitation to detect chemical or radiological threats in areas that are difficult to access. (U.S. Marine Corps video by Cpl. Esgar Rojas)
keywords: nuclear, biological, radiological, CBRN, Okinawa Japan, 3rd Mar. Div., CBRN Marines, chemical threats, 3D MAR DIV, Defense Platoon, radiological threats, U.S. Marines, Okinawa, Japan, battalion, Headquarters, chemical, defense, Camp Hansen, 3rd Marine Division

transcript.text: - The exercise we did today was a CWMB-type mission
for an unknown chemical agent
in a facility.
The objective today was to exercise our training standards
and our ability to make a restricted access
using vertical means
to extricate victims
and to address and remove an unknown chemical hazard.
(dramatic music)
- The fact that we are the only unit in the Marine Corps
that has rappelling and you have the rope capability
with rope rescue, it makes it so at any point,
wherever in the world, if we're needed,
we can be there.
We can be deployed,
and we can respond to any incident,
above any other platoon,
just cause they don't have the capability.
So, what's great about our platoon
is it makes it so we're able
to be able to deploy at any time,
and then leave without any extra support.
(dramatic music)
